question: Why are illustrators and animators closing their Etsy shops over its new terms?

rungs.question: Why are illustrators and animators closing their Etsy shops now?
rungs.answer: Etsy's terms, effective 16 December, add an explicit right for Etsy and its third-party partners and vendors to use seller content to develop, train, test and improve AI. The sellers posting goodbyes name that clause as the reason, and some are leaving in the holiday season, giving up income.

evidence.quote: Starting December 16, the agreement explicitly gives Etsy and its third-party partners and vendors permission to use content uploaded by sellers to train and improve AI systems.
The business decided to leave the platform due to changes in Etsy’s terms of use.
“I would say I’m losing 20 percent of my yearly income,” he said. “It’s a few mortgage payments.”

counter.text: Not every seller is leaving: Creative Bloq reports some feel trapped because Etsy is their main income, and Cybernews says the total number who left is unknown. Quotes: "Others who have yet to take the leap say they feel trapped because they depend on Etsy as their main source of income" (creativebloq.com); "It is not yet known how many sellers have left Etsy because of these changes." (cybernews.com).

rungs.question: Why does Etsy's promise not to train copycat models fail to settle sellers?
rungs.answer: The promise covers Etsy's own models, but the clause also names third-party partners and vendors, and Etsy has not said whether those partners may use seller content to train AI for purposes unrelated to Etsy. Sellers read that phrase as open-ended.

evidence.quote: He said Etsy uses security tools to detect and limit unauthorized scraping, while its Terms prohibit unauthorized use of marketplace content for AI training, but did not clarify whether authorized partners can use seller content to train models for applications unrelated to Etsy.
That said, the vague terms leave open just how its partners and vendors might use that same content.
By Etsy, by its 'partners and vendors,' a phrase roomy enough to fit pretty much anyone,” shared the post.

counter.text: Etsy's chief executive wrote that the update was not meant to enable copycat models: "It was not meant to enable us to train AI models for the purpose of creating copycats of your items. We do not and will not do that." (arstechnica.com). Etsy's own note and community post could not be read (403 and script-only page), so its exact wording on partners was not checked at source.

rungs.question: Why do sellers not simply opt out and keep selling?
rungs.answer: There is no switch. The terms point to opt-out rights in the Privacy Policy, but neither policy gives US sellers a general way to keep their content out of training while still selling. One seller was told to email Etsy's data protection officer; others were told to close their accounts.

evidence.quote: While the updated Terms refer to applicable opt-out rights, neither policy identifies a general mechanism specifically allowing US sellers to exclude their listing photos, descriptions or other uploaded content from AI training while continuing to sell on Etsy.
Instead, they need to contact the company’s data protection officer via email and ask that their data not be used to train AI.
Some users who have already contacted the company about the matter have said they had been advised to close their accounts if they disagreed with Etsy’s terms.

counter.text: An email route to the data protection officer does exist per Cybernews, and Value Added Resource notes EU and UK sellers may have additional rights to object, though not necessarily over all creative content. The privacy policy itself was unreadable (403), so the opt-out text was not checked at source.

rungs.question: Why does closing a shop not obviously end the matter?
rungs.answer: The licence sellers already grant in Section 5 is perpetual and irrevocable, so removing listings or closing a shop may not end Etsy's permission over content already uploaded. Etsy has not said how it treats such content in training data or models. Only one source sets this out.

evidence.quote: Because the license is perpetual and irrevocable, simply removing a listing or closing a shop may not terminate Etsy's contractual permission to use previously uploaded content, although the company has not clarified how it handles that material in AI training datasets or models.
Section 5 already included a perpetual licence allowing Etsy to reproduce, modify, distribute and create derivative works from user content.

counter.text: Value Added Resource also says the existing licence was already broad, so the new wording does not necessarily mean training starts now: "the new language does not necessarily mean the company is beginning AI training with that information for the first time." Scope: the five sources; Etsy's terms page was unreadable (403).

rungs.question: Why did Etsy write the AI training right into its terms at all?
rungs.answer: Etsy's stated reason is to improve models behind seller tools, search and recommendations, and fraud detection. The same update bars outsiders from training on Etsy data without permission and gives Etsy control over AI shopping agents, which points to keeping that data for Etsy and its chosen partners. The sources do not say that outright.

evidence.quote: "The recent update to our Terms and Privacy Policy regarding AI Models is intended to enable Etsy to use user-generated content to improve LLMs that strengthen our marketplace in service of our community, like AI-powered tools that make running a shop easier for sellers, surfacing the most relevant items for buyers, and technology that helps detect fraud."

He provided some examples of how the platform is training AI, including to identify potentially fraudulent accounts and related listings, to understand inventory, to help buyers find items and tailored recommendations and to build tools to help sellers run their businesses more efficiently.

The updated Terms extend those restrictions, expressly prohibiting third parties from using content or data obtained from Etsy's services to develop, train, fine-tune, evaluate, benchmark or otherwise contribute to AI systems without the company's permission, regardless of whether that information was collected manually or through automated tools.

counter.text: Cybernews raises a different reading, that Etsy may want human-made listings as fresh training data: "the company’s upcoming changes regarding AI training suggest that it may be seeking to use human-created listings as fresh training data for its AI models." That is a suggestion, not a documented motive. Value Added Resource says Etsy did not clarify whether it was already training on this content.

landing.shows: The ladder runs from a single added sentence in Etsy's terms to sellers walking away. Etsy's stated uses are its own tools, search and fraud checks, and it promises no copycat models. But the clause also covers unnamed partners and vendors, there is no in-settings opt-out for US sellers, and the existing licence is perpetual. That leaves leaving as the only control sellers can see. Etsy's reason for writing the right in, beyond its stated uses, is not documented.
landing.open_question: If a seller's licence to Etsy is perpetual and its partners go unnamed, what does closing a shop actually take back?
